interpretation: Sparse benchmark instances have low density (mean ~0.3535) and localized cyclic substructures (mean fraction of vertices in nontrivial SCCs: ~72.71%). LOLIB instances, by contrast, have near-complete density (mean ~0.4542) with essentially all vertices in one large SCC (mean fraction: ~98.67%). This structural contrast is consistent with the observed performance: SCC-local refinement (IPSNS) targets isolated cyclic subgraphs effectively on sparse instances, while matrix-based pairwise-ordering (DRMacIver/FAS) aligns naturally with fully dense complete-ordering instances.
